topic: Binary Rhythms: Unlocking the Towers of Hanoi
target_audience: Middle school and high school students

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Language of Bits
lecture_lines: Binary uses only zero and one as switches.
Each position represents a power of two.
Five is four plus one, or one-zero-one. [Asset: bin_5]
animations: Visualize a bit as a light bulb switching between ON (#FFFF00) and OFF (#FFFFFF).
Show a sequence of three bits representing numbers 0 to 7 in binary.
Highlight the transition from bit 0 to bit 1 using a smooth color fade.

sections.title: The Towers of Hanoi Challenge
lecture_lines: Three rods, n-disks; a classic challenge.
Larger disks cannot sit on smaller ones.
Exponential growth: more disks mean many steps. [Asset: hanoi_moves]
animations: Display three stacked disks of varying sizes (#FF5733, #33FF57, #3357FF).
Show a move operation of the smallest disk to an adjacent peg.
Animate the full recursive move sequence for three disks at reduced speed.

sections.title: Mapping Moves to Binary
lecture_lines: Disk moves match binary counting patterns.
Each bit position controls one specific disk. [Asset: bit_to_disk]
Counting in binary reveals the move order. [Asset: binary_table]
animations: Display a binary number next to its corresponding disk movement instruction.
Map the bit change sequence (000, 001, 010) to specific disk jumps.
Show the disks moving in synchronization with the binary counter.

sections.title: Application: The Binary Automaton
lecture_lines: No more guessing: solve any disk count.
Deterministic steps make the path clear.
The automaton shows the next disk move. [Asset: binary_clock]
animations: Show a simple gear-based mechanism translating binary to physical motion.
Animate the mechanism stepping through the state transitions of the disks.
Highlight the final state change once the binary counter reaches completion.

sections.title: Summary & Complexity Analysis
lecture_lines: Total moves follow the two-to-n pattern.
Binary math simplifies this complex puzzle.
Exponential growth at work in ten disks. [Asset: growth_graph]
animations: Display the total number of moves for 3 disks as a formula 2^n - 1.
Show the exponential growth of moves as the disk count increases.
Summarize the time complexity as O(2^n) on screen.
